name: Gilneas
summary: Beyond the Greymane Wall, Gilneas keeps the world at a distance. The human kingdom lies on a rugged peninsula south of Silverpine Forest, sealed away after the Second War by King Genn Greymane.

sections.title: A Nation Withdrawn
sections.body:
Gilneas once ruled the waves among the human kingdoms and traced its line to Arathor, the ancient human empire. King Genn Greymane entered the Second War reluctantly. He believed his realm could defend itself without ties to foreign powers.

Bitter over Gilnean deaths and unwilling to help pay for internment camps holding captured orcs, he broke with the Alliance of Lordaeron. Then he ordered a great stone wall along Gilneas's northern frontier to shield the kingdom from calamity beyond its borders.

sections.title: The Severed Frontier
sections.body: The Greymane Wall left two villages exposed. Its builders anchored the ramparts to natural mountain passes, leaving Ambermill and Pyrewood Village beyond the gate on the northern side. When the Scourge crossed Lordaeron during the Third War, King Greymane refused pleas for aid. He barred human refugees from entering, and the villages beyond the wall faced plague and undead alone.

sections.title: A Looming Shadow
sections.body: During the Third War, Dalaran archmage Arugal summoned feral worgen to aid the Kirin Tor against the Scourge. The beasts slew the undead, then turned on the wizards and besieged Baron Silverlaine's keep. They spread through the shadows of Silverpine. Gilneas remains sealed behind its gates and treacherous sea reefs, while eerie rumors and silence shroud the kingdom.

aliases: can you go past greymane wall
faq.answer: No. Gilneas lies behind the Greymane Wall at Silverpine Forest's southern border. Its iron gate is barred, and sheer sea cliffs and treacherous reefs guard the peninsula's coast.

faq.q: Why was the Greymane Wall built?
faq.answer: King Genn Greymane believed Gilneas could stand on its own and resented spending lives and resources to aid other human nations. After the Second War, bitter over debts, internment camps and foreign conflicts, he built the wall to isolate Gilneas from the rest of Lordaeron.

faq.q: What happened to Pyrewood Village and Ambermill?
faq.answer: The Greymane Wall followed defensible mountain ridges, leaving Pyrewood Village and Ambermill on its northern side, outside the kingdom. Once the gates were sealed, the villages were cut off from Gilneas.

faq.q: Is Gilneas part of the Alliance?
faq.answer: No. Genn Greymane withdrew Gilneas from the Alliance of Lordaeron. The kingdom has no diplomatic ties, military treaties or trade with Stormwind, Ironforge or any other Alliance power.

faq.q: What connection does Arugal have to Gilneas?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Dalaran archmage Arugal summoned feral worgen to aid the Kirin Tor against the Scourge. They slew the undead, then turned on the wizards, overran Shadowfang Keep and spread through Silverpine, driving Arugal mad.
King Genn Greymane rules Gilneas. He fiercely guards the kingdom's independence, leaving the world beyond its gates to fend for itself.

angles.text: As a human of Lordaeron or Stormwind, you may see Gilneas as a bitter reminder of how pride and isolation broke the unity of the Seven Kingdoms before the Third War.
As a Forsaken, you patrol southern Silverpine and watch the great gate. A whole human kingdom remains alive and hostile just across your border.
As a mage, you know Archmage Arugal's summoning beneath the Greymane Wall as a grim warning of magic turned to war without restraint.
